subject: Vocabulary
topic: Synonyms in Context — Choose the Best-Fit Synonym for the Underlined Word in Sentence (W13 B1)

questions.stem: The judge's decision to ACQUIT the defendant surprised many who had followed the trial closely.
questions.explanation: B is correct. ACQUIT = to formally declare someone not guilty of a criminal charge; to free from blame or accusation. EXONERATE = to officially absolve someone from blame or criminal charges. Both mean to clear of wrongdoing. Trap: PUNISH = opposite; CONDEMN = opposite (declare guilty); INCRIMINATE = to make someone appear guilty (opposite of acquit).

questions.stem: The scientist's EMPIRICAL findings were based on years of careful observation and experimentation.
questions.explanation: B is correct. EMPIRICAL = based on observation, experiment or experience rather than theory or pure logic. EXPERIMENTAL = derived from or relating to experiment and observation. Both contrast with theoretical or abstract knowledge. Trap: THEORETICAL = opposite (based on theory, not observation); HYPOTHETICAL = based on assumptions/what might be true (not yet tested); PHILOSOPHICAL = concerned with abstract thought.

questions.stem: The politician's RHETORIC was impressive but contained very few concrete policy proposals.
questions.explanation: C is correct. RHETORIC = the art of effective or persuasive speaking or writing, often with the connotation of language used for effect rather than content. ORATORY = the art or practice of formal public speaking; elaborate or formal speech. In context (impressive but lacking substance), both capture the sense of skilled but potentially hollow speech. Trap: EVIDENCE = opposite of the implication (the speaker lacked substance); LOGIC = suggests reasoned argument (rhetoric can be illogical, appealing to emotion).

questions.stem: After years of LANGUISHING in poverty, the village finally received government aid.
questions.explanation: B is correct. LANGUISH = to be or become weak or feeble; to suffer from being in an unpleasant situation for a long time; to fail to make progress. SUFFERING = experiencing pain, distress or difficulty. In context ('languishing in poverty'), the best contextual synonym is SUFFERING (experiencing the hardship of poverty over time). Trap: FLOURISHING = thriving (antonym); EMERGING = coming into view or developing (neutral, lacks the suffering element); PROGRESSING = moving forward (opposite of languishing).

questions.stem: The board SANCTIONED the new budget after a lengthy debate among members.
questions.explanation: C is correct. SANCTION has two opposite meanings (a Janus word): (1) to officially approve or permit something; (2) a penalty imposed for violating a rule. In context ('sanctioned the new budget after a debate'), SANCTION clearly means APPROVED (gave official permission). PAPER-SETTER TRAP: PENALISED = the second meaning of 'sanction' (punishment) — the examiner uses this to see if you pick context-based meaning or the other meaning. Always use context: 'sanctioned a budget' = approved it.

questions.stem: Her TENACIOUS grip on the project saw it through despite numerous obstacles.
questions.explanation: B is correct. TENACIOUS = holding firm; not readily giving up; persistent and determined. PERSISTENT = continuing firmly in a course despite difficulty or opposition. In context (grip on project saw it through despite obstacles), PERSISTENT is the best synonym. Trap: RELUCTANT = unwilling (opposite — tenacious implies willingness to continue); TEMPORARY = lasting for a limited time (tenacious implies sustained effort, the opposite of temporary).

questions.stem: The CEO was CANDID about the company's financial difficulties during the press conference.
questions.explanation: C is correct. CANDID = truthful and straightforward; frank; not concealing anything. FORTHRIGHT = direct and outspoken; going straight to the point without evasion. In context (CEO being candid about difficulties), FORTHRIGHT captures the direct, frank communication. Trap: EVASIVE = avoiding directness (opposite of candid); AMBIGUOUS = open to more than one interpretation (candid is the opposite — clear and direct); CAUTIOUS = being careful, which can accompany evasiveness (opposite of candid).

questions.stem: The BENEVOLENT industrialist donated a large sum to build schools in rural areas.
questions.explanation: B is correct. BENEVOLENT = well-meaning and kindly; disposed to do good; generous. PHILANTHROPIC = of or relating to the desire to promote the welfare of others; generous with money for good causes. In context (donating to build schools), PHILANTHROPIC is the best contextual synonym. Trap: MISERLY = mean and unwilling to spend (antonym); INDIFFERENT = having no interest or sympathy (antonym); PRAGMATIC = dealing with things sensibly (no charitable connotation).

questions.stem: The EPHEMERAL beauty of cherry blossoms makes them all the more precious to those who view them.
questions.explanation: C is correct. EPHEMERAL = lasting for a very short time; transitory. TRANSIENT = passing away quickly; lasting only a short time. In context (beauty that is precious BECAUSE it is brief), TRANSIENT captures the fleeting, short-lived quality. Trap: PERMANENT = opposite; EXTRAORDINARY = remarkable (does not capture the short-lived quality); VIBRANT = bright and energetic (describes quality of beauty, not its duration). The SSC frequently tests EPHEMERAL because students confuse it with 'external' or 'ethereal'.

questions.stem: The new policy was CONTENTIOUS, with different stakeholders holding diametrically opposing views.
questions.explanation: B is correct. CONTENTIOUS = causing or likely to cause argument; controversial. CONTROVERSIAL = giving rise to public disagreement; disputed. Both perfectly fit the context (stakeholders holding opposing views). Trap: UNAMBIGUOUS = clear and without doubt (opposite — contention arises from ambiguity or conflicting interests, but the word itself means the policy causes disagreement, not that it is unclear); CONSENSUAL = relating to or involving consensus (antonym — if contentious, there is no consensus); CONSTRUCTIVE = serving a useful purpose (no relation to the sense of conflict).
